# FynMesh

> FynMesh is an open source micro frontend framework built on Module Federation and Rollup.

---

# Why FynMesh

URL: https://www.fynmesh.fyi/why-fynmesh

FynMesh is an open source micro frontend framework built on Module Federation and Rollup. A team picks it when several apps, built and deployed separately, have to live on one page and cooperate. This page lists what FynMesh does differently and where it does not fit.

## Apps join the page without wiring

When a FynApp loads, it joins the page's shared scope. The scope is one named scope, called `fynmesh`, and loading plus initializing the app is the whole act of joining. No app passes a scope to another app.

Nobody keeps a list of who shares with whom. If app A and app B both ship React and both ask for a compatible range, the loader hands both the same copy. Add a third app and nothing in A or B changes.

This matters most when different teams release on different days. A team ships its app and the page picks it up. There is no host config to edit and no remote map to keep in sync.

## Apps ask for apps by version range

Most tools let a package ask for a library as `react@^19`. FynMesh lets a page ask for an app the same way: `fynapp-x1@^2`. The host supplies a registry resolver that maps a name and a range to a manifest URL.

The consumer states the range once. The host decides which deployment satisfies it, and it can change that decision without rebuilding any consumer.

A side effect is that releases of one app can share a name on the same page. One consumer can ask for `^1.0.0` while another asks for `^2.0.0`, and each gets a matching release. Teams can move consumers over one at a time. The guide [Upgrade React incrementally](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/guides/upgrade-react-incrementally) shows a case of this.

You do need a real resolver for this. The default resolver that ships with the kernel maps a name to `/<name>/dist/fynapp.manifest.json` and does not look at the range. See [How FynMesh works](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/how-it-works) for the host code.

## Apps that cooperate

It reads each app's manifest and builds a dependency graph. Apps boot in dependency order, so a provider is ready before its consumers run. The kernel also detects cycles in the graph.

Every app follows the FynUnit lifecycle. An app can implement `initialize`, `execute`, `suspend`, `resume` and `shutdown`. The kernel calls `suspendFynApp`, `resumeFynApp` and `shutdownFynApp` and tracks each app's state. A failed bootstrap is isolated, so siblings keep running.

Middleware handles concerns that cross apps, such as a shared theme or a page layout. One FynApp provides a middleware and others declare it with `useMiddleware`. A middleware can also take over how an app executes, which is how the [shell demo](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/shell) builds its layout.

FynBus handles messaging. Apps publish and subscribe, and they can send a request that waits for a handler that has not loaded yet. The platform stamps the sender of each message, and an app's subscriptions are dropped when it shuts down.

Middleware and FynBus are add-on bundles. A page that does not need them can load the core kernel alone.

## Frameworks mix without a bridge

Each FynApp is a plain federated container. The kernel runs its `main` export and does not care what renders the UI. The demo runs React 18, React 19, Vue, Preact, Solid, Svelte and Marko on the same loader.

There is no per-framework bridge package and no adapter to install when you add a framework. The scaffolding tool, `create-fynapp`, has templates for eight frameworks and accepts any other name.

## You can see what happened

The Federation Inspector is an in-page panel. It shows each shared module, who supplied it and which ranges asked for it. It reads the loader's state directly, so the apps need no instrumentation.

It also lists named issues, such as a range that nothing satisfies or a singleton loaded in several copies. When a page picks an unexpected React version, you can see why. Under the panel, `Federation.__I()` returns the same data to your own code. Details are in the [Federation Inspector docs](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/docs/federation-inspector).

## Built on Rollup

You build each FynApp with Rollup and `rollup-plugin-federation`. The plugin emits the container entry and embeds the app's manifest in it. The kernel reads that manifest without an extra request. FynMesh does not need webpack. The guide [Micro frontends with Rollup](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/guides/micro-frontends-with-rollup) walks through a build.

## When FynMesh may not fit

Be aware of these limits today.

- There is no server-side rendering integration. FynApps render in the browser. The kernel has a Node stub that does not run federation.
- There is no federated TypeScript types feature. A consumer declares each provider with one `declare module` line, which types its imports as `any`, or writes precise declarations by hand.
- Routing is not part of the kernel. A shell app owns routing.
- The Federation Inspector is an in-page panel. There is no browser extension.

If your pages must render on the server, or you need typed contracts across apps with no hand-written declarations, weigh those limits first.

## Where to go next

- [Features](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/features) shows each capability with a diagram.
- [Live demos](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/demos) lists the demo pages.
- [Getting started](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/docs/getting-started) creates your first FynApp.
- [FAQ](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/faq) answers common questions.

---

# How FynMesh Works

URL: https://www.fynmesh.fyi/how-it-works

FynMesh is an open source micro frontend framework built on Module Federation and Rollup. Each app is built on its own into a federated container. A small kernel in the browser finds those containers by name and version range, loads them in dependency order and runs them.

The sections below follow one app from build to runtime.

## 1. Build

A FynApp is a normal Rollup project with one extra plugin, `rollup-plugin-federation`. You give the plugin a `name`, the modules the app `exposes` and the modules it lists under `shared`.

```js
federation({
  name: "fynapp-1",
  filename: "fynapp-entry.js",
  exposes: { "./main": "./src/main.ts" },
  shared: { react: { singleton: true, semver: "^19.0.0" } },
});
```

The plugin generates a container entry. It collects the shared modules and who imports them, then writes metadata about what the build exposes and shares. The output is ES module code in the SystemJS register format. See the [rollup-plugin-federation docs](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/docs/rollup-plugin-federation).

The build also emits a manifest. It is written twice with the same content: embedded in `fynapp-entry.js` as `__FYNAPP_MANIFEST__`, and as `dist/fynapp.manifest.json`. The kernel has to fetch the entry anyway, so reading the embedded copy costs no extra request. The JSON file is a fallback.

The manifest lists the app's name and version, its exposes, what it provides and consumes as shared, and which other apps it imports from.

## 2. The registry resolver

The host page loads the kernel as a script and gets a global, `fynMeshKernel`. There is no class to construct. The host then sets a registry resolver. The resolver takes an app name and an optional semver range and returns the manifest URL.

```ts
const kernel = globalThis.fynMeshKernel;

kernel.setRegistryResolver(async (name, range) => ({
  name,
  version: range ?? "latest",
  url: `https://cdn.example.com/${name}/dist/fynapp.manifest.json`,
  distBase: `https://cdn.example.com/${name}/dist/`,
}));

await kernel.loadFynAppsByName(
  [
    { name: "fynapp-1" },
    { name: "fynapp-x1", range: "^1.0.0" },
    { name: "fynapp-x1", range: "^2.0.0" },
  ],
  { concurrency: 4, preload: 1 },
);
```

This host asks for two ranges of `fynapp-x1`. The resolver returns a distinct `version` for each, which keys the dependency graph. A real resolver would query a registry. The kernel ships a demo resolver that ignores the range.

`loadFynAppsByName` rejects if the batch cannot be planned, for example when no resolver is set. One app that fails to load does not abort the batch.

## 3. Dependency graph and boot order

The kernel reads each manifest and builds a graph. Edges come from the manifest fields `requires`, `import-exposed` and `shared-providers`. It detects cycles, then loads apps in topological batches. `concurrency` caps how many load at once, and `preload` sets how deep to preload dependencies.

An app that needs a middleware or a shared module from another app waits until that provider is ready. If a provider never arrives, the wait ends after 30 seconds with a `FYNAPP_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT` event.

## 4. Shared modules and semver ranges

All containers on the page join one named share scope, `fynmesh`. Loading and initializing a container registers what it provides. No container passes a scope to another one.

Each importer declares the range it accepts. When an app imports `react`, the runtime, `federation-js`, looks for a loaded version that satisfies every range that applies. If one fits, the app reuses it. If none fits, the app loads its own copy.

`singleton: true` asks for one instance across all containers. When the constraints conflict, `federation-js` warns instead of throwing.

This is how React 18 and React 19 coexist. An app asking for `^18.0.0` and an app asking for `^19.0.0` each get a matching copy. Read [Share dependencies with semver](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/guides/share-dependencies-semver) and the [federation-js docs](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/docs/federation-js) for more.

## 5. The FynUnit lifecycle

An app's `main` export is a FynUnit. It can be a plain function, an object with `execute`, or a class instance with `initialize` and `execute`. The kernel validates the shape and throws if there is no `execute`.

```ts
import { useMiddleware, type FynUnit, type FynUnitRuntime } from "@fynmesh/kernel";

const unit: FynUnit = {
  initialize(runtime: FynUnitRuntime) {
    return { status: "ready" };
  },
  execute(runtime: FynUnitRuntime) {
    const tokens = runtime.middlewareContext.get("design-tokens");
    console.log(`${runtime.fynApp.name} theme:`, tokens?.theme);
  },
  shutdown(runtime: FynUnitRuntime) {
    console.log(`${runtime.fynApp.name} shutting down`);
  },
};

export const main = useMiddleware(
  {
    mw: import("fynapp-design-tokens/middleware/design-tokens/design-tokens", {
      with: { type: "fynapp-middleware" },
    }),
    config: { theme: "fynmesh-default", cssCustomProperties: true },
  },
  unit,
);
```

The kernel calls `initialize`, then `execute`, then signals `FYNAPP_BOOTSTRAPPED`. A mounted app can also implement `suspend`, `resume` and `shutdown`. The kernel calls them from `suspendFynApp`, `resumeFynApp` and `shutdownFynApp`.

Each app has a state you can read with `getFynAppState` or `listFynAppStates`. A failure in one app emits `FYNAPP_BOOTSTRAP_FAILED` and does not stop the others.

## 6. Middleware

Middleware covers concerns that cross apps. A provider is a FynApp that exposes a `./middleware*` module and exports objects whose names start with `__middleware__`. A consumer declares what it needs with `useMiddleware`, as in the sample above.

For each middleware the kernel runs `setup`, then `apply`. `apply` puts an API into `runtime.middlewareContext`. A middleware marked for auto-apply can also override how a unit executes. The first one that says yes wins.

The build turns the `import()` in a declaration into an id string, so the middleware is resolved through the same manifest and graph as everything else.

## 7. FynBus

FynBus is the messaging layer. Apps emit and subscribe to events, and they can send a request to a handler. The platform stamps the sender of each message. A request waits for a handler that has not loaded yet. An app's subscriptions are cleaned up when the app shuts down.

An app reaches the bus as `runtime.bus`, and the host reaches it as `kernel.bus`.

## 8. Kernel add-ons

The core kernel resolves manifests, builds the graph, loads, bootstraps and manages lifecycle and events. Everything else is an add-on bundle.

- The middleware add-on holds the middleware registry, auto-apply and overrides.
- The bus add-on provides FynBus.
- The telemetry add-on adds `kernel.setTelemetry`.
- The dev-overlay add-on shows bootstrap failures on the page, in development only.
- The AMD add-on serves federated modules to legacy RequireJS bundles under the ids they already ask for. It is a working prototype, shown in the [legacy RequireJS demo](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/legacy-amd) and the [guide](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/guides/legacy-requirejs-on-module-federation).

Load core first, then any add-ons. Each add-on installs itself into `fynMeshKernel` and throws if core is missing. Without the middleware add-on, a unit runs as plain `initialize` then `execute`, and a unit that declares middleware gets a console warning. The README for the [kernel](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/docs/kernel) lists the bundle files, and the [kernel API](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/api/) covers the types.

## 9. Inspection

`Federation.__I()` returns a snapshot of shared-module resolution. For each chunk and share key it shows the ranges the importers declared, the ranges resolution applied and the versions available. The Federation Inspector draws this in a panel on the page, with modules, graph, shares, issues, middleware and FynApps views. See the [inspector docs](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/docs/federation-inspector).

## Next steps

Follow [Getting started](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/docs/getting-started) to build a first app. The [FynApp contract](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/docs/fynapp-contract) describes what the kernel expects from one. The [live demo](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/demo) shows the pieces running together.

---

# FynMesh FAQ

URL: https://www.fynmesh.fyi/faq

FynMesh is an open source micro frontend framework built on Module Federation and Rollup. These answers cover what it is, how versions and sharing work, how to build an app and how to debug a page. Each answer links to a longer page when there is one.

## Basics

### What is FynMesh?

FynMesh is an open source micro frontend framework built on Module Federation and Rollup. It lets you build one page from several apps that are built and deployed on their own.

It provides a build plugin, a loader that shares dependencies by semver range, and a kernel that boots apps in dependency order. See [Why FynMesh](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/why-fynmesh) and [How FynMesh works](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/how-it-works).

### What is a FynApp?

A FynApp is one independently built and deployed app. It is a Rollup project that produces a federated container and a manifest.

Its `main` export is a FynUnit, which the kernel runs. The [FynApp contract](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/docs/fynapp-contract) describes what the kernel expects.

### Does FynMesh need webpack?

No. FynMesh builds with Rollup and `rollup-plugin-federation`, and the runtime loads SystemJS modules. The guide [Module Federation without webpack](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/guides/module-federation-without-webpack) shows the setup.

### Which frameworks work?

React 18 and 19, Vue, Preact, Solid, Svelte and Marko all run in the demo. Each app is a plain federated container, so no bridge or adapter is needed.

`create-fynapp` has templates for eight frameworks: `react`, `react18`, `preact`, `vue`, `solid`, `svelte`, `marko` and `vanilla`. Any other name gets a generic skeleton that builds as is.

### Is FynMesh free and open source?

Yes. The code is on GitHub under the Apache-2.0 license, and the packages are on npm. You can use, modify and ship it under the terms of that license.

### Do I need a shell app?

No. The kernel can load FynApps on any page. A shell is one pattern, built with middleware, and the [shell demo](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/shell) shows it.

### Does FynMesh handle routing?

No. The kernel has no routing. A shell app owns routing, if you need it. The [shell demo](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/shell) shows a layout built that way.

## Versions and sharing

### Can two React versions run on one page?

Yes. An app that asks for `^18.0.0` gets React 18, and an app that asks for `^19.0.0` gets React 19. The loader keeps each loaded version as a separate provider.

The [live demo](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/demo) runs both. The guide [Run multiple React versions](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/guides/run-multiple-react-versions) explains the setup.

### How are shared dependencies resolved?

Each app declares what it shares and the semver range it accepts. At runtime the loader picks a loaded version that satisfies the ranges that apply to the import and reuses it.

If no loaded version fits, the app loads its own copy. The guide [Share dependencies with semver](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/guides/share-dependencies-semver) goes through examples.

### What does singleton do?

`singleton: true` asks for one instance of a module across all containers. Use it for libraries that break when two copies exist.

When the ranges conflict, `federation-js` warns instead of throwing. The Federation Inspector reports a singleton that loaded in several copies.

### Does every app have to use the same version of a shared library?

No. Each app lists a semver range. Apps whose ranges agree share one copy, and a range that needs a different major gets its own.

### Can two versions of the same app run together?

Yes. A page can ask for `fynapp-x1@^1.0.0` and `fynapp-x1@^2.0.0`, and each request gets a matching release. The resolver must return a distinct `version` for each one.

This needs a registry resolver that reads the range. The default resolver that comes with the kernel ignores it. See the host code in [How FynMesh works](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/how-it-works), and the guide [Upgrade React incrementally](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/guides/upgrade-react-incrementally).

### Do apps need to know about each other to share?

No. An app joins the shared scope, named `fynmesh`, when it loads. Nobody keeps a list of who shares with whom.

An app that imports a module from another app, such as a middleware, does name that app. The kernel uses that to load the provider first.

### Can legacy RequireJS bundles use federated React?

Yes. Webpack AMD bundles that list React or a UI kit as externals can load them from federation, under the RequireJS ids they already ask for. The bundles are not rebuilt. A kernel add-on routes those ids to a FynApp that serves the libraries. The add-on is a working prototype in the repo. See the guide [Serve shared libraries to legacy RequireJS bundles](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/guides/legacy-requirejs-on-module-federation).

### Can legacy widgets move to a new React major without a rebuild?

Yes, as long as their code runs on that major. Each RequireJS context chooses the old common bundle or the federated one, so one group of widgets can move to React 19 while another stays on React 18. The [legacy RequireJS demo](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/legacy-amd) runs both on one page.

## Building FynApps

### How do I start a new FynApp?

Install the scaffolding tool with `fyn global add create-fynapp`, then run `create-fynapp --name my-app --framework react`. It creates `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `rollup.config.ts` and starter source files.

The [getting started guide](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/docs/getting-started) covers the rest.

### What does a build produce?

A build produces `fynapp-entry.js` and `fynapp.manifest.json` in `dist/`. The manifest is also embedded in the entry file.

The kernel reads the embedded copy first, because it has to fetch the entry anyway. The JSON file is a fallback.

### How do apps talk to each other?

Through middleware APIs and FynBus. FynBus lets apps publish and subscribe to events and send requests to handlers. The platform stamps the sender of each message.

A request waits for a handler that has not loaded yet. An app's subscriptions are dropped when it shuts down.

### What is middleware?

Middleware is code that one FynApp provides and other apps use. It handles cross-app concerns such as a shared theme or a page layout.

A consumer declares it with `useMiddleware`. The kernel runs the middleware's `setup` and `apply` steps before the app's `execute`, and `apply` puts an API into `runtime.middlewareContext`. A middleware can also take over how an app executes, which the shell demo uses for its layout.

### Can I use FynMesh without the middleware or the bus?

Yes. Both are add-on bundles. Load `fynmesh-kernel-core` alone and a unit runs as plain `initialize` then `execute`.

A unit that declares middleware gets a console warning when the middleware add-on is missing. The [kernel docs](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/docs/kernel) list the bundles.

### Does FynMesh share TypeScript types across apps?

No. There is no federated type generation today. A consuming app types its remote imports with one `declare module "fynapp-design-tokens/*";` line per provider, which gives them the type `any`.

You can write precise declarations by hand, or share a contract package between teams. The kernel exports its own types from `@fynmesh/kernel`, including `FynUnit` and `FynUnitRuntime`.

## Running and debugging

### How do I see which version an app got?

Call `Federation.__I()` in the console or open the in-page Federation Inspector. Both list each shared module, its providers and the ranges that asked for it.

For FynApps, `kernel.listFynAppStates()` returns the name, version and status of each. The [inspector docs](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/docs/federation-inspector) describe the panels.

### What happens when a FynApp fails to load?

The rest of the batch carries on. `loadFynAppsByName` does not abort when one app fails, and the kernel emits `FYNAPP_LOADED` with `detail.ok` set to false.

A failure while running an app emits `FYNAPP_BOOTSTRAP_FAILED` and leaves the other apps running. An app that waits for a dependency that never arrives emits `FYNAPP_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT` after 30 seconds. The dev-overlay add-on shows bootstrap failures on the page in development.

### Does FynMesh support server-side rendering?

No. There is no server-side rendering integration today. FynApps render in the browser.

If you need server rendering, plan for that before you pick FynMesh. The kernel has a Node stub, but it does not run federation, so it is not a path to server rendering.

---

# Getting Started: Create a FynApp

URL: https://www.fynmesh.fyi/docs/getting-started

`create-fynapp` provides two commands:

- `create-fynapp` creates a React FynApp in the current directory.
- `cfa` builds and checks an existing FynApp or installs the bundled coding-agent skills.

**FynMesh:** [Website](https://www.fynmesh.fyi) · [Demo](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/demo) · [Shell demo](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/shell)

## Installation

Install the released commands globally with fyn:

```bash
fyn global add create-fynapp
```

If the commands are not on `PATH`, run `fyn global setup-path` and follow its
shell instructions.

To work on this package in the FynMesh monorepo:

```bash
cd dev-tools/create-fynapp
fyn install
fyn run build
```

## Create a FynApp

The app is created in the directory you run the command from. At the root of
the FynMesh monorepo it is created under `demo/` instead, which is where that
repository keeps its FynApps.

```bash
create-fynapp --name my-app --framework react
```

`--framework` takes **any** framework name. Eight ship a complete template —
`react`, `react18`, `preact`, `vue`, `solid`, `svelte`, `marko`, `vanilla` —
and scaffold a working app for it. Any other name (`qwik`, `lit`, `alpine`, …)
scaffolds the framework-generic skeleton: it installs, builds and passes
`cfa check` as it stands, and comes with an `AGENT-TODO.md` checklist for the
coding agent that converts it. Nothing is rejected for being unfamiliar.

Options:

- `--name, -n <string>`: package and federation name.
- `--framework, -f <string>`: any framework name; the eight above have templates.
- `--dir, -d <string>`: directory to create (defaults to the name).
- `--skip-install`: create files without running `fyn install`.

The command creates `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `rollup.config.ts`, and
starter source files. Register a new demo app separately as described in
[`agent/GUIDE.md`](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/docs/fynapp-guide).

## Work with an existing FynApp

Run `cfa` from the FynApp directory, or pass `--dir`.

### Build

```bash
cfa build
cfa build --watch
cfa build --dir demo/my-app
```

Options:

- `--dir, -d <string>`: target directory (defaults to the current directory).
- `--watch, -w`: rebuild when source files change.
- `--minify, -m`: enable minified output.

### Check build output

```bash
cfa check
cfa check --no-build
```

`cfa check` builds with the local Rollup binary, then checks for
`dist/fynapp-entry.js` and a parseable `dist/fynapp.manifest.json` with the
required identity and `./main` expose. `--no-build` checks an existing
`dist/`.

### What a build emits

`dist/` gets JSON as well as JavaScript, and the files are not interchangeable:

- **`fynapp.manifest.json`** — this FynApp's public contract: identity, `exposes`,
  `consume-shared` / `provide-shared`, `import-exposed`, `shared-providers`. Other
  FynApps' builds read it off disk to discover who provides their shared modules, so
  **build order matters** — a dependency built after its consumer leaves the consumer's
  `shared-providers` empty.
- **`__FYNAPP_MANIFEST__`** inside `fynapp-entry.js` — the same manifest embedded in the
  entry, which is how the kernel reads it without an extra request. Middleware
  registration depends on it and has no fallback.
- **`federation.json`** — build plumbing: expose-to-chunk mapping and share config. Optional;
  nothing at runtime needs it.
- **`federation.bundles.json`** — only when the build's chunks were combined into one file:
  the map of which file carries which module, which a host reads to preload the file that
  will really be fetched.
- **`__collected_shares.json`** — debug output. Nothing reads it.

Full reference, including every consumer:
[notes/BUILD-ARTIFACTS.md](https://github.com/jchip/fynmesh/blob/main/notes/BUILD-ARTIFACTS.md).

### Install coding-agent skills

```bash
cfa install-skills
cfa install-skills --dir path/to/project
cfa install-skills --force
```

This opt-in command copies the bundled `fynapp-modify` and
`fynapp-migrate-kernel` skills into `<project>/.claude/skills/`.

## Authoring references

- [FynApp guide](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/docs/fynapp-guide)
- [FynApp contract](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/docs/fynapp-contract)
- [Kernel migration playbook](https://github.com/jchip/fynmesh/blob/main/dev-tools/create-fynapp/agent/MIGRATION.md)
- [Curated examples](https://github.com/jchip/fynmesh/tree/main/dev-tools/create-fynapp/examples)

## Development checks

```bash
fyn run build
fyn test
```

# FynApp Guide: Create or Modify an App

URL: https://www.fynmesh.fyi/docs/fynapp-guide

This package supports two distinct workflows. Pick the right one.

| You want to… | Do this |
|--------------|---------|
| **Create a new FynApp** | Run the static `create-fynapp` CLI (§1). Mechanical, no code understanding needed. |
| **Modify an existing FynApp** | You're a coding agent — follow [`CONTRACT.md`](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/docs/fynapp-contract), copy from the [FynMesh examples](https://github.com/jchip/fynmesh/tree/main/dev-tools/create-fynapp/examples), then `cfa check` (§2). |
| **Update FynApps to a changed kernel API** | Follow [`MIGRATION.md`](https://github.com/jchip/fynmesh/blob/main/dev-tools/create-fynapp/agent/MIGRATION.md). |

> **Claude Code skills (opt-in).** This package bundles two skills under
> [`../skills/`](https://github.com/jchip/fynmesh/tree/main/dev-tools/create-fynapp/skills) — `fynapp-modify` and `fynapp-migrate-kernel`. They
> are **not** installed automatically. To make them available in a project, run
> `cfa install-skills` — it copies them into `<project>/.claude/skills/`
> (`--force` to overwrite). `.claude/` is typically gitignored, so each user
> decides whether to install them.

---

## 1. Create a new FynApp (CLI — static scaffold)

From the monorepo root:

```bash
create-fynapp --name my-fynapp --framework react
# options: --name/-n, --framework/-f (any framework name; templates:
#            react | react18 | preact | vue | solid | svelte | marko | vanilla),
#          --dir/-d (defaults to the name), --skip-install
```

**`--framework` accepts any name.** Eight frameworks ship a hand-authored
template and scaffold a complete working app. Any other name — `qwik`, `lit`,
`alpine`, whatever you can work with — scaffolds the framework-generic skeleton
instead, plus an `AGENT-TODO.md` in the new app. That scaffold is not a stub:
it installs, builds and passes `cfa check` before you touch it, so you convert
it one step at a time from a green baseline. Converting it is a **modify** task
(§2) and `AGENT-TODO.md` is its checklist.

Run from the monorepo root this scaffolds `demo/my-fynapp/`; run anywhere else
it scaffolds `my-fynapp/` in the current directory. Either way from static
templates: `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `rollup.config.ts` (the
`createFynAppRollupConfig` factory form), and a starter `src/`. It does **not**
reason about your code — it just stamps out a known-good skeleton that already
conforms to [`CONTRACT.md`](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/docs/fynapp-contract).

### Register the new app in the demo server

The scaffold creates the app but the demo server must be told about it:

1. **`demo/demo-server/templates/components/fynapp-loader.html`** — add your app
   to the `features` map: `"my-fynapp": true` (`true` = eager, `"lazy"` =
   button-triggered, omit = off).
2. **`demo/demo-server/src/dev-proxy.ts`** — add a path mapping so the dev server
   can find its files:
   ```ts
   [ { path: "/my-fynapp" },
     { protocol: "file", path: Path.join(__dirname, "../../my-fynapp") } ],
   ```

Then from the repo root: `fyn bootstrap` (build all) and `fyn start`
(→ `http://localhost:3000/demo.html`).

> Editing `fynapp-loader.html`/`dev-proxy.ts` is a *trivial config edit* — do it
> mechanically. Anything beyond stamping the skeleton (real components,
> middleware, rendering logic) is a **modify** task → §2.

---

## 2. Modify an existing FynApp (coding agent)

Modifying requires understanding the code, so it is your job, not a code-mod's.
The loop:

1. **Read the contract.** [`CONTRACT.md`](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/docs/fynapp-contract) is authoritative for the
   `FynUnit` lifecycle, `rollup.config.ts`, middleware consume/provide, render
   results, and package/tsconfig shape.
2. **Copy a pattern.** Find the closest match in the [FynMesh examples](https://github.com/jchip/fynmesh/tree/main/dev-tools/create-fynapp/examples):
   - `react-minimal` — standalone React app.
   - `middleware-consumer` — consume another app's middleware.
   - `middleware-provider` — author a middleware.
   - `vanilla` — framework-agnostic.
   The working demo apps `demo/fynapp-6-react` and `demo/fynapp-design-tokens`
   are the fuller, real-world versions.
3. **Make the surgical edit** to `src/` (and, if adding an exposed module or a
   dependency, the *trivial* config edits to `rollup.config.ts` / `package.json`).
4. **Check** — the change is not done until this passes:
   ```bash
   cd demo/<fynapp> && cfa check
   ```
   `cfa check` builds via rollup and checks the federation output
   (`dist/fynapp-entry.js` + a valid `dist/fynapp.manifest.json` exposing
   `./main`). Use `--no-build` to check an existing `dist/`.
5. If the app renders UI, also load it in the demo (`fyn start`) to confirm
   runtime behavior — types and manifest passing does not prove it renders.

### Common modifications (all → CONTRACT.md sections)

- Add/adjust rendering → `FynUnit.execute` + render results (CONTRACT §2, §5).
- Consume a middleware → `useMiddleware` + `middlewareContext.get` (CONTRACT §4).
- Provide a middleware → `__middleware__` export + `setup`/`apply` (CONTRACT §6);
  add the `./middleware/*` expose to `rollup.config.ts` (CONTRACT §3).
- Add a dependency → `package.json` (trivial); React apps use public `react`/`react-dom`.

---

## 3. Build helpers exported by `create-fynapp`

`rollup.config.ts` files import these from `create-fynapp`:

| API | Purpose |
|-----|---------|
| `createFynAppRollupConfig(opts)` | **Preferred** whole-config factory |
| `setupFynAppOutputConfig()` | Standard `dist/` SystemJS output |
| `setupDummyEntryPlugins()` | Virtual entry federation requires |
| `setupReactFederationPlugins(cfg)` / `setupFederationPlugins(cfg)` | Federation + manifest |
| `setupReactAliasPlugins()` | Local-demo alias: `react` → `esm-react` |
| `setupMinifyPlugins()` | Terser (production only) |
| `fynappDummyEntryName`, `fynappEntryFilename`, `env` | Constants for the low-level form |
| `checkFynApp`, `runCheck` | Programmatic output check (what `cfa check` calls) |

Debug the build with `DEBUG=create-fynapp`.

---

# The FynApp Contract

URL: https://www.fynmesh.fyi/docs/fynapp-contract

**Audience: LLM coding agents modifying an existing FynApp.** This is the
authoritative, type-anchored contract for what a FynApp *is*. The kernel types and
selected lifecycle/runtime members described here are anchored by
`../src/fynapp-contract.ts`, which is compiled on every build. Additive and
behavioral changes still require a kernel API review. When you change a FynApp,
conform to this contract and then run `cfa check` (see §8).

> Scope note: creating a *new* FynApp is a static, mechanical operation — run the
> `create-fynapp` CLI (see `GUIDE.md`). This document is for *modifying* an
> existing app, which requires understanding the code. `--framework` accepts any
> name: one without a template scaffolds a generic skeleton that already
> conforms to this contract, plus an `AGENT-TODO.md`. Finishing that conversion
> is a *modify* task, so it is governed by this document.

---

## 1. Anatomy

```
<fynapp>/
├── package.json          # "type":"module"; build script "rollup -c"; deps below
├── rollup.config.ts      # THE defining file — federation name, exposes, framework
├── tsconfig.json
├── src/
│   ├── main.ts | main.tsx   # exports `const main` = a FynUnit  (the entry)
│   └── ...                   # App.tsx, middleware/, hooks/, styles.css, …
└── dist/                 # build output
    ├── fynapp-entry.js       # the federation entry the kernel loads (fixed name);
    │                         #   also carries the manifest as `__FYNAPP_MANIFEST__`
    ├── fynapp.manifest.json  # generated manifest (name/version/exposes/…)
    └── federation.json       # build plumbing: expose→chunk map, share config
```

The two manifest copies hold identical content and both matter — see
[build artifacts](https://github.com/jchip/fynmesh/blob/main/notes/BUILD-ARTIFACTS.md).

Two invariants hold for **every** FynApp:
1. `rollup.config.ts` declares a federation `name` and exposes `./main`. For
   `framework: "react"` the helper injects `./main` automatically; for
   non-React frameworks you must list it explicitly (see §3).
2. `src/main.ts` (or `.tsx`) exports `const main` implementing `FynUnit`.

There is **no** `"fynapp"` field in `package.json`; identity lives in
`rollup.config.ts` (`name`) and the generated `dist/fynapp.manifest.json`.

---

## 2. The `FynUnit` contract — what `src/main.ts` exports

Source: `@fynmesh/kernel` → `core/kernel/src/types.ts:121`.

```ts
export interface FynUnit {
  __middlewareMeta?: MiddlewareUseMeta<unknown>[];
  initialize?(runtime: FynUnitRuntime):
    | Promise<{ status: string; mode?: string }>
    | { status: string; mode?: string };
  execute(runtime: FynUnitRuntime): Promise<any> | any;   // ONLY required method
  shutdown?(runtime: FynUnitRuntime): Promise<void> | void;
  suspend?(runtime: FynUnitRuntime): Promise<void> | void;
  resume?(runtime: FynUnitRuntime): Promise<void> | void;
  [key: string]: any;
}
```

| Method | When | Returns |
|--------|------|---------|
| `initialize(runtime)` | first, before middleware applies | `{ status: "ready" \| "defer", mode?, deferOk? }` |
| `execute(runtime)` | after middleware is ready | a render result (see §5) |
| `shutdown(runtime)` | on unload | `void` — clean up (unmount, remove listeners) |
| `suspend(runtime)` | when a mounted app is paused | `void` — pause timers/subscriptions |
| `resume(runtime)` | when a suspended app is restored | `void` — resume paused work |

`main` may be a **class instance** implementing `FynUnit`, a **plain object**
with at least `execute`, or the return value of **`useMiddleware([...], unit)`**.
A bare function export is also accepted (kernel wraps it as `{ execute: fn }`).

`FynModule` / `FynModuleRuntime` are **deprecated aliases** of `FynUnit` /
`FynUnitRuntime` — do not introduce them in new code.

### `FynUnitRuntime` — the `runtime` argument

`core/kernel/src/types.ts:82`:

```ts
export type FynUnitRuntime = {
  fynApp: FynApp;                                     // { name, version, packageName, entry, exposes, … }
  middlewareContext: Map<string, Record<string, any>>; // read consumed middleware here
  bus?: FynBus;                                       // inter-FynApp messaging
  [key: string]: any;
};
```

`runtime.bus` is the optional per-app messaging facade. It supports ephemeral
`emit`/`on`/`once`, request-response with `request`/`handle`, and isolated named
channels. Subscriptions return an unsubscribe function; release it from
`shutdown` or `suspend` as appropriate. State that late-loading apps must observe
belongs in the middleware state registry, not the bus.

There is **no `runtime.kernel`**. To reach the kernel from a FynUnit, use
`globalThis.fynMeshKernel`.

---

## 3. The `rollup.config.ts` contract

The **default and preferred** form is the high-level factory (this is what
current demo apps use — e.g. `demo/fynapp-6-react/rollup.config.ts`):

```ts
import { createFynAppRollupConfig } from "create-fynapp";

export default createFynAppRollupConfig({
  name: "my-fynapp",           // federation identity — REQUIRED
  framework: "react",          // "react" | "vanilla" | "vue" | … (drives aliases/externals)
  typescript: true,
  exposes: {},                 // "./main" is added automatically
  // extraPlugins: [ newRollupPlugin(postcss)() ],  // for CSS, etc.
});
```

`createFynAppRollupConfig` (`../src/rollup-config-factory.ts`) assembles, in
fixed order: dummy-entry → node-resolve → `extraPlugins` → federation → react
demo alias (only with `reactPackages: "esm-adapters"`) → `extraPluginsAfter` →
typescript → minify (prod).
It always emits SystemJS output to `dist/` with share scope `fynmesh`, input
`[fynappDummyEntryName, fynappEntryFilename]`.

**What the federation configuration guarantees** (`../src/index.ts`):
- For React, the preferred factory always includes `"./main": "./src/main.ts"`.
  The generic low-level `setupFederationPlugins` does **not** inject it — add
  `"./main": "./src/main.ts"` to `exposes` yourself.
- React frameworks consume `react`, `react-dom`, and `react-dom/client` as
  singleton shared packages. Source and `package.json` use those standard public
  packages directly.
- Repository demos that intentionally use the local ESM adapters opt in with
  `reactPackages: "esm-adapters"`. The low-level `setupReactFederationPlugins`
  and `setupReactAliasPlugins` helpers exist for that demo mode.
- `renderDynamicImport` enables the `import(..., { with: { type: "fynapp-middleware" } })`
  syntax used by consumers (§4).
- `enrichManifest` + `emitFederationMeta` produce the manifest — both the copy
  embedded in `fynapp-entry.js` and `dist/fynapp.manifest.json`. `enrichManifest`
  is what computes `import-exposed` and `shared-providers`, the fields the kernel
  resolves dependencies from.

**Escape hatch (advanced):** the low-level form — call
`setupDummyEntryPlugins`, `setupReactFederationPlugins`/`setupFederationPlugins`,
`setupReactAliasPlugins`, `setupMinifyPlugins` yourself and assemble the
`defineConfig([...])` array (see `demo/fynapp-react-middleware/rollup.config.ts`).
Use only when the factory's ordering/options are insufficient.

To expose extra modules (e.g. a middleware), add to `exposes`:

```ts
exposes: { "./middleware/greeting": "./src/middleware/greeting.ts" },
```

---

## 4. Consuming middleware

Declare needs with `useMiddleware` (`core/kernel/src/use-middleware.ts:22`),
then read the provider's published API from `runtime.middlewareContext`:

```ts
import { useMiddleware } from "@fynmesh/kernel";

export const main = useMiddleware(
  {
    // @ts-ignore — TS can't type module-federation remote containers
    mw: import("fynapp-design-tokens/middleware/design-tokens/design-tokens",
      { with: { type: "fynapp-middleware" } }),
    config: { theme: "fynmesh-default", cssCustomProperties: true },
  },
  new MyUnit(),
);
```

- The import specifier is `<package>/<exposeModule>/<middlewareName>` — e.g.
  `fynapp-design-tokens` + expose `middleware/design-tokens` + middleware
  `design-tokens`.
- `config` is passed to the provider verbatim as `cc.meta.config`. The string
  `"consume-only"` is a common convention meaning "consumer, don't provide".
- Pass an **array** to use several middlewares.
- In `execute`, read the API: `const dt = runtime.middlewareContext.get("design-tokens"); dt?.api?.setTheme(...)`.
- If the provider may load later, return `{ status: "ready", deferOk: true }` from
  `initialize` and handle a missing entry gracefully (re-render on the
  `MIDDLEWARE_READY` kernel event — see §6).

---

## 5. Render results (returned from `execute`)

The shell-layout middleware defines the result contract
(`demo/fynapp-shell-mw/src/middleware/shell-layout.ts`). The common cases:

```ts
// FynApp renders itself into a DOM node it owns:
{ type: "self-managed", target: HTMLElement, cleanup?: () => void }

// The shell renders the FynApp (when shell-managed):
{ type: "component-factory", componentFactory: (React) => ({ component, props }) }

// Cannot render:
{ type: "no-render", message: string }
```

A FynApp that supports both modes branches on
`runtime.middlewareContext.get("shell-layout")?.isShellManaged` inside `execute`.

---

## 6. Authoring a middleware (provider)

A **provider** is a FynApp that exposes one or more `./middleware/*` modules. The
kernel discovers a middleware by finding, in an exposed module, an export whose
name starts with `__middleware__` (marker `MIDDLEWARE_EXPORT_PREFIX`,
`core/kernel/src/util.ts`).

The exported instance implements `FynAppMiddleware`
(`core/kernel/src/types.ts:177`):

```ts
export type FynAppMiddleware = {
  name: string;
  autoApplyScope?: ("all" | "fynapp" | "middleware")[];   // auto-apply w/o useMiddleware
  shouldApply?(fynApp: FynApp): boolean;
  setup?(cc: FynAppMiddlewareCallContext): Promise<{ status: string; share?: any } | void>;
  apply?(cc: FynAppMiddlewareCallContext): Promise<void> | void;
  // execution-override hooks (used by shell-layout):
  canOverrideExecution?(fynApp: FynApp, fynUnit: FynUnit): boolean;   // note arg order
  overrideInitialize?(cc: FynAppMiddlewareCallContext): Promise<{ status: string; mode?: string }>;
  overrideExecute?(cc: FynAppMiddlewareCallContext): Promise<void>;
};
```

Phases:
1. **`setup(cc)`** — one-time per consuming FynApp. Check `cc.meta.config`.
   Return `{ status: "ready" }`, or `{ status: "defer" }` to postpone the
   consumer's `execute` until readiness is signalled. Signal readiness for
   deferred flows with `await cc.kernel.signalMiddlewareReady(cc, { name, status: "ready" })`.
2. **`apply(cc)`** — integrate. Publish your API for consumers:
   `cc.runtime.middlewareContext.set(this.name, api)`.

`FynAppMiddlewareCallContext` (`core/kernel/src/types.ts:162`) gives you
`{ meta, fynUnit, fynApp, reg, runtime, kernel, status }`.

Minimal shape:

```ts
import type { FynAppMiddleware, FynAppMiddlewareCallContext } from "@fynmesh/kernel";

class GreetingMiddleware implements FynAppMiddleware {
  readonly name = "greeting";
  async setup(cc: FynAppMiddlewareCallContext) {
    await cc.kernel.signalMiddlewareReady(cc, { name: this.name, status: "ready" });
    return { status: "ready" };
  }
  apply(cc: FynAppMiddlewareCallContext) {
    cc.runtime.middlewareContext.set(this.name, { greet: (n: string) => `Hello, ${n}!` });
  }
}
export const __middleware__Greeting = new GreetingMiddleware();
```

**Cross-FynApp shared state**: use the reactive registry
`cc.kernel.getMiddlewareRegistry("global")` → `provide(key, data)` /
`lookup(key)` / `waitFor(key, timeoutMs)` (backed by `ObservableState`). See
`demo/fynapp-react-middleware` (`basic-counter`) for the provider/consumer
dual-mode pattern.

A provider still needs `src/main.ts`; if it *only* provides middleware, that file
is just `export {};` (because `./main` is always exposed).

---

## 7. package.json / tsconfig contract

`package.json` essentials:
```jsonc
{
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": { "build": "rm -rf dist && rollup -c", "dev": "rollup -c -w" },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@fynmesh/kernel": "^1.1.5", "create-fynapp": "^1.1.7",
    "rollup": "^4.9.1", "rollup-plugin-federation": "^1.0.0",
    "rollup-wrap-plugin": "^1.0.0", "typescript": "^5.2.2"
    // React apps also: react, react-dom, @rollup/plugin-*, @types/react, rollup-plugin-postcss
  }
}
```
React apps depend on the standard public `react`/`react-dom` packages.

`tsconfig.json`: ESNext/ES2020 module, `moduleResolution: "bundler"`,
`jsx: "react"`, `declaration: true`,
`include: ["src/**/*"]`. Copy an existing app's `tsconfig.json`.

---

## 8. Check (always, after any change)

```bash
cd <fynapp> && cfa check      # builds via rollup + checks the federation output
```

`cfa check` (implemented in `../src/check-fynapp.ts`) builds the app and
asserts `dist/fynapp-entry.js` and a parseable `dist/fynapp.manifest.json` with
`name`, `version`, and the `./main` expose. Use `cfa check --no-build` to check
an existing `dist/`. A change is not done until this passes.

---

## Sources of truth — and stale sources to IGNORE

**Trust:** `@fynmesh/kernel` (types re-exported via `core/kernel/src/index.ts`),
`../src/fynapp-contract.ts` (the compiled anchor), and the working demo apps
`demo/fynapp-6-react` (consumer) and `demo/fynapp-design-tokens` (provider).

**Do NOT trust (stale/aspirational):**
- `core/kernel/examples/simple-usage.ts` — references a non-existent
  `new Kernel(...)` / `loadFynapp` / `getModule` API.
- Any claim that `runtime.kernel` exists — it does not (use `globalThis.fynMeshKernel`).
- `canOverrideExecution` argument order in `execution-override-architecture.md`
  (doc shows `(fynUnit, fynApp)`); the real signature is `(fynApp, fynUnit)`.
- The `{ info: MiddlewareInfo }` form of a consumer declaration — the runtime uses
  the `{ mw: import(...), config }` form shown in §4.
- Any `{ middleware: import(...) }` consumer declaration, or `cc.reg.middleware` /
  `cc.fynMod` — the key is `mw`, and `fynMod` was removed (see MIGRATION.md).

---

# FynMesh Kernel API and Concepts

URL: https://www.fynmesh.fyi/docs/kernel

The FynMesh kernel is a generic lifecycle engine for micro-frontend orchestration. It manages FynApp loading, middleware coordination, and bootstrap dependencies while remaining agnostic to specific frameworks or rendering strategies.

**FynMesh:** [Website](https://www.fynmesh.fyi) · [Demo](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/demo) · [Shell demo](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/shell)

## Overview

The kernel provides:

1. **FynApp Loading**: Load and initialize FynApps via Module Federation
2. **Middleware System**: Extensible middleware for cross-cutting concerns
3. **Bootstrap Coordination**: Dependency resolution between FynApps
4. **Lifecycle Management**: Setup, apply, execute phases for FynUnits

### What the kernel reads about a FynApp

Everything the kernel knows before running a FynApp comes from that FynApp's **manifest**,
which the build emits in two copies with identical content: embedded in `fynapp-entry.js` as
`__FYNAPP_MANIFEST__`, and as `dist/fynapp.manifest.json`. The embedded copy is preferred
because the entry file is fetched regardless, so reading it costs no extra request.

The manifest fields that drive loading are `requires`, `import-exposed`, and
`shared-providers` — `manifest-resolver.ts` walks them to build the dependency graph, and
`module-loader.ts` re-reads `import-exposed` off the container to register middleware from
provider FynApps. That second read has **no fallback**; the rest of the chain does.

**→ [Build artifacts reference](https://github.com/jchip/fynmesh/blob/main/notes/BUILD-ARTIFACTS.md)** for the exact shapes, the
four-tier resolution chain, and what each fallback does and does not recover.

## Installation

```bash
fyn add @fynmesh/kernel
```

## Core Concepts

### FynUnit

A `FynUnit` is the execution contract for a FynApp's main module. It can be:

- A simple function
- An object with `execute` method
- A class instance with `initialize` and `execute` methods
- Any of the above wrapped with `useMiddleware()`

```typescript
// Simple function
export const main = (runtime: FynUnitRuntime) => {
  // execution logic
};

// Object with execute
export const main = {
  initialize(runtime: FynUnitRuntime) {
    return { status: "ready" };
  },
  execute(runtime: FynUnitRuntime) {
    return { type: "component-factory", componentFactory: () => MyComponent };
  }
};

// With middleware (see "Using Middleware" for the full declaration)
export const main = useMiddleware(
  {
    mw: import("fynapp-design-tokens/middleware/design-tokens/design-tokens",
      { with: { type: "fynapp-middleware" } }),
    config: {}
  },
  {
    execute(runtime) {
      return { type: "react-component", component: MyApp };
    }
  }
);
```

### FynUnitRuntime

The runtime context provided to FynUnits during execution:

```typescript
type FynUnitRuntime = {
  fynApp: FynApp;
  middlewareContext: Map<string, Record<string, any>>;
  bus?: FynBus; // present when the bus add-on is installed
  [key: string]: any; // middleware may add more fields
};
```

The kernel itself is the global `fynMeshKernel`. It is not a field of the runtime.

### Middleware

Middleware intercept and extend FynUnit execution:

```typescript
type FynAppMiddleware = {
  name: string;

  // Auto-apply without useMiddleware(); explicit useMiddleware() always works
  autoApplyScope?: ("all" | "fynapp" | "middleware")[];
  shouldApply?(fynApp: FynApp): boolean;

  // Setup phase - initialize middleware state
  setup?(context: FynAppMiddlewareCallContext): Promise<{ status: string; share?: any } | void>;

  // Apply phase - provide APIs to FynUnit
  apply?(context: FynAppMiddlewareCallContext): Promise<void> | void;

  // Override execution - take control of FynUnit execution
  canOverrideExecution?(fynApp: FynApp, fynUnit: FynUnit): boolean;
  overrideInitialize?(context: FynAppMiddlewareCallContext): Promise<{ status: string; mode?: string }>;
  overrideExecute?(context: FynAppMiddlewareCallContext): Promise<void>;
};
```

### Execution Paths

The kernel supports 2 execution paths:

**Path 1: Simple Function**
```typescript
export const main = (runtime: FynUnitRuntime) => {
  // Kernel wraps as { execute: fn }
};
```

**Path 2: FynUnit Object (with or without middleware)**
```typescript
// Without middleware - auto-apply middleware only
export const main = {
  execute(runtime) { /* ... */ }
};

// With middleware - full middleware coordination
export const main = useMiddleware({ mw: import(/* ... */), config: {} }, {
  execute(runtime) { /* ... */ }
});
```

### Execution Flow

```
1. Load FynApp entry module
2. Validate FynUnit (check for execute method or function)
3. Load middleware dependencies (from __middlewareMeta)
4. For each middleware:
   a. setup() - Initialize middleware
   b. apply() - Inject APIs into middlewareContext
5. Call FynUnit.initialize() (or middleware override)
6. Call FynUnit.execute() (or middleware override)
7. Signal bootstrap complete (FYNAPP_BOOTSTRAPPED)
```

### Runtime Validation

The kernel validates FynUnit shape at runtime:

```typescript
// Valid FynUnits:
export const main = (runtime) => {};           // Function
export const main = { execute(runtime) {} };   // Object with execute
export const main = new MyClass();             // Class instance with execute

// Invalid - will throw error:
export const main = {};                        // No execute method
export const main = { run() {} };              // Wrong method name
```

## Bundles and Add-ons

The core kernel loads, orders and bootstraps FynApps. Everything else is an add-on.

| Add-on | Adds |
| --- | --- |
| middleware | `registerMiddleware`, `getMiddleware`, `getMiddlewareRegistry`, `signalMiddlewareReady`, auto-apply, execution overrides |
| bus | `kernel.bus` and per-app `runtime.bus` |
| telemetry | `kernel.setTelemetry(config)` |
| dev-overlay | an on-page panel for bootstrap failures (dev only) |

Browser bundles in `dist/`:

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `fynmesh-browser-kernel.{dev,min}.js` | core and every add-on; the dev one also has the overlay |
| `fynmesh-kernel-core.{dev,min}.js` | core only |
| `fynmesh-kernel-middleware.{dev,min}.js` | middleware add-on |
| `fynmesh-kernel-bus.{dev,min}.js` | bus add-on |
| `fynmesh-kernel-telemetry.{dev,min}.js` | telemetry add-on |
| `fynmesh-kernel-dev-overlay.dev.js` | dev overlay add-on |

Load core first. Each add-on installs itself into `globalThis.fynMeshKernel` when it runs, and throws if core is missing.
Order among add-ons does not matter, and loading one twice is harmless.

```html
<script src="fynmesh-kernel-core.min.js"></script>
<script src="fynmesh-kernel-middleware.min.js"></script>
<script src="fynmesh-kernel-bus.min.js"></script>
```

To ship one file, concatenate them with core first:

```sh
cat fynmesh-kernel-core.min.js fynmesh-kernel-middleware.min.js fynmesh-kernel-bus.min.js > kernel.js
```

Without the middleware add-on, a FynUnit runs as plain `initialize` then `execute`.
A unit that declares middleware gets a console warning.

## Usage

### Basic Kernel Setup

A host page loads the kernel as a script. The browser bundle creates the global `fynMeshKernel`. There is no class to construct.

Load order matters. SystemJS comes first, then federation-js, then the kernel bundle. Each one reads the global the previous one defines. Script paths depend on your deployment.

```html
<script src="/path/to/system.min.js"></script>
<script src="/path/to/federation-js.min.js"></script>
<script src="/path/to/fynmesh-browser-kernel.min.js"></script>
```

`fynmesh-browser-kernel.{dev,min}.js` includes core and every add-on, so it is the simplest choice. For a smaller page, load `fynmesh-kernel-core.min.js` plus only the add-ons you need. See [Bundles and Add-ons](#bundles-and-add-ons).

The kernel ships with a demo resolver that maps a name to `/<name>/dist/fynapp.manifest.json`. A real host sets its own resolver, then asks for FynApps by name and optional semver range.

```html
<script>
  (async () => {
    fynMeshKernel.setRegistryResolver(async (name, range) => ({
      name,
      version: "1.0.0", // resolved version; keys the dependency graph
      url: `https://cdn.example.com/${name}/dist/fynapp.manifest.json`,
      distBase: `https://cdn.example.com/${name}/dist/` // optional
    }));

    await fynMeshKernel.loadFynAppsByName(
      [{ name: "fynapp-1" }, { name: "fynapp-x1", range: "^2.0.0" }],
      { concurrency: 4, preload: 1 }
    );
  })();
</script>
```

The resolver returns a `RegistryResolverResult`: `name`, `version`, `url` (manifest), and optional `distBase`. Give each distinct version its own `version` so the dependency graph can tell them apart.

`loadFynAppsByName` takes `LoadFynAppsOptions`:

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `concurrency` | Max FynApps loaded in parallel. Default 4. |
| `preload` | A number (dependency depth to preload, default 1) or a `PreloadStrategy` object: `depth`, `priority`, `priorityByDepth`, `disabled`. |

It rejects when the batch cannot be planned, for example when no resolver is set. A single FynApp that fails to load does not abort the batch.

### Using Middleware

A FynApp declares the middleware it needs with `useMiddleware(meta, unit)`. Each declaration has an `mw` import and a `config`. The import must carry the `fynapp-middleware` attribute, and the specifier is `<package>/<exposeModule>/<middlewareName>`. The build turns it into an id string the kernel can read.

```typescript
import { useMiddleware } from "@fynmesh/kernel";

const unit = {
  initialize(runtime) {
    return { status: "ready" };
  },
  execute(runtime) {
    const tokens = runtime.middlewareContext.get("design-tokens");
    return { type: "react-component", component: MyComponent };
  }
};

export const main = useMiddleware(
  {
    mw: import("fynapp-design-tokens/middleware/design-tokens/design-tokens",
      { with: { type: "fynapp-middleware" } }),
    config: { theme: "fynmesh-default", cssCustomProperties: true }
  },
  unit
);
```

`config` is passed to the provider as `context.meta.config`. Pass an array to use several middleware.

The provider is a remote FynApp, so TypeScript has no types for its modules. Declare each provider once in a `.d.ts` file of the consumer, and every import from it type-checks:

```typescript
// src/remotes.d.ts
declare module "fynapp-design-tokens/*";
```

Each declaration is a `MiddlewareDeclaration`. Besides `{ mw, config }`, the kernel accepts a bare `mw` import, and `{ info: { name, provider, version? }, config }`, which looks up a middleware that is already registered by name and provider.

### Creating Middleware

A middleware provider is a FynApp that exposes a `./middleware*` module. The kernel scans every expose whose key starts with `./middleware`. It registers each export whose name starts with `__middleware__`.

```typescript
import type { FynAppMiddleware, FynAppMiddlewareCallContext } from "@fynmesh/kernel";

class GreetingMiddleware implements FynAppMiddleware {
  name = "greeting";

  async setup(context: FynAppMiddlewareCallContext) {
    return { status: "ready" };
  }

  apply(context: FynAppMiddlewareCallContext) {
    // Provide an API to the FynUnit
    context.runtime.middlewareContext.set(this.name, {
      greet: (who: string) => `Hello, ${who}!`
    });
  }
}

export const __middleware__Greeting = new GreetingMiddleware();
```

Expose the module in the provider's federation config, for example `exposes: { "./middleware/greeting": "./src/middleware/greeting.ts" }`. A consumer then imports `<package>/middleware/greeting/greeting`. A provider still needs its own `src/main.ts`.

### Middleware Override Priority

A middleware can take over execution of a FynUnit. Only auto-applied middleware are asked, so set `autoApplyScope` on the middleware. **First-come-first-serve** applies:
- The first middleware with `canOverrideExecution(fynApp, fynUnit) === true` wins
- That middleware's `overrideInitialize()` and `overrideExecute()` are called
- Other middleware still run setup/apply phases

```typescript
// Shell middleware overrides every FynApp it applies to
autoApplyScope = ["fynapp", "middleware"];

canOverrideExecution(fynApp, fynUnit) {
  return true; // Takes control of rendering
}
```

## API Reference

The full reference, generated from the types, is at [www.fynmesh.fyi/api](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/api/modules/_fynmesh_kernel). The summary below covers what most hosts and FynApps use.

### FynMeshKernel

The global `fynMeshKernel` implements this interface. `@fynmesh/kernel` exports it as a type.

```typescript
interface FynMeshKernel {
  events: FynAppEventTarget;   // emitter of kernel events, has on() and once()
  version: string;             // kernel version
  shareScopeName: string;      // federation share scope name

  use(addon: KernelAddon): void;                                  // install an add-on, no-op if already installed
  initRunTime(data: FynMeshRuntimeData): FynMeshRuntimeData;      // set the kernel runtime data
  setRegistryResolver(resolver: RegistryResolver): void;          // map name and range to a manifest URL

  loadFynAppsByName(                                              // load FynApps and their dependencies
    requests: Array<{ name: string; range?: string }>,
    options?: LoadFynAppsOptions
  ): Promise<void>;
  loadFynApp(baseUrl: string, loadId?: string): Promise<FynApp | null>; // load and bootstrap one FynApp, null on failure
  loadFynAppBasics(fynAppEntry: FynAppEntry): Promise<FynApp>;    // load entry, config and main, run nothing
  bootstrapFynApp(fynApp: FynApp): Promise<void>;                 // run a loaded FynApp

  shutdownFynApp(name: string): Promise<boolean>;                 // call shutdown() and remove the FynApp
  suspendFynApp(name: string): Promise<boolean>;                  // call suspend() on a mounted FynApp
  resumeFynApp(name: string): Promise<boolean>;                   // call resume() on a suspended FynApp
  getFynAppState(name: string): FynAppState | undefined;          // "name" or "name@version"
  listFynAppStates(): FynAppState[];                              // state of every tracked FynApp

  emitAsync(event: CustomEvent): Promise<boolean>;                // dispatch an event on the kernel
}
```

Each add-on adds its own API to `fynMeshKernel` once installed:

- `MiddlewareKernelApi`: `registerMiddleware`, `getMiddleware`, `getMiddlewareRegistry`, `signalMiddlewareReady`
- `BusKernelApi`: `bus`
- `TelemetryKernelApi`: `setTelemetry(config?)`

### Kernel Configuration

The kernel has no constructor config. The browser bundle creates it for you.

- Registry: `setRegistryResolver(resolver)`
- Batch loading: `LoadFynAppsOptions` on `loadFynAppsByName`
- Telemetry: `setTelemetry({ transport?, maxBufferSize? })` from the telemetry add-on
- Bootstrap timeout: fixed at 30 seconds

### FynUnit

```typescript
interface FynUnit {
  __middlewareMeta?: MiddlewareUseMeta<unknown>[];
  initialize?(runtime: FynUnitRuntime): Promise<{ status: string; mode?: string }> | { status: string; mode?: string };
  execute(runtime: FynUnitRuntime): Promise<any> | any;
  shutdown?(runtime: FynUnitRuntime): Promise<void> | void; // on shutdownFynApp
  suspend?(runtime: FynUnitRuntime): Promise<void> | void;  // on suspendFynApp
  resume?(runtime: FynUnitRuntime): Promise<void> | void;   // on resumeFynApp
}

// Deprecated aliases (for backwards compatibility)
type FynModule = FynUnit;
type FynModuleRuntime = FynUnitRuntime;
```

### useMiddleware

```typescript
function useMiddleware<T extends FynUnit = FynUnit>(
  meta: MiddlewareUseMeta<unknown> | MiddlewareUseMeta<unknown>[],
  unit: T
): T;

// For middleware that don't need a FynUnit
const noOpFynUnit: FynUnit;
```

## Kernel Events

The kernel emits events for monitoring:

| Event | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `FYNAPP_LOADING` | FynApp load started (from `loadFynAppsByName`) |
| `FYNAPP_LOADED` | FynApp load attempt ended, `detail.ok` is false on failure |
| `FYNAPP_BOOTSTRAPPED` | Bootstrap completed |
| `FYNAPP_BOOTSTRAP_FAILED` | Bootstrap failed (error isolated) |
| `FYNAPP_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT` | A deferred bootstrap waited too long for its dependencies |
| `FYNAPP_SUSPENDED` | FynApp suspended |
| `FYNAPP_RESUMED` | FynApp resumed |
| `FYNAPP_SHUTDOWN` | FynApp shut down |
| `MIDDLEWARE_READY` | A middleware signaled readiness (middleware add-on) |

## Error Handling

The kernel isolates errors to prevent one FynApp from crashing others:

- Failed FynApps emit `FYNAPP_BOOTSTRAP_FAILED` event but don't crash
- Bootstrap timeouts emit `FYNAPP_BOOTSTRAP_TIMEOUT` after 30s
- Middleware failures are logged but don't block other FynApps

## Architecture

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      FynMesh Kernel                         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  ┌─────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌───────────────────┐  │
│  │   Module    │  │  Middleware  │  │    Bootstrap      │  │
│  │   Loader    │  │  Executor    │  │   Coordinator     │  │
│  └─────────────┘  └──────────────┘  └───────────────────┘  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                    Middleware Layer                         │
│  ┌─────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐  ┌───────────────────┐  │
│  │   Shell     │  │   Design     │  │      React        │  │
│  │   Layout    │  │   Tokens     │  │     Context       │  │
│  └─────────────┘  └──────────────┘  └───────────────────┘  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                      FynApps (FynUnits)                     │
│  ┌─────────┐ ┌─────────┐ ┌─────────┐ ┌─────────┐          │
│  │ React   │ │  Vue    │ │ Svelte  │ │ Marko   │  ...     │
│  │ 18/19   │ │  3.x    │ │  4.x    │ │  5.x    │          │
│  └─────────┘ └─────────┘ └─────────┘ └─────────┘          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Design Principles

1. **Generic Lifecycle Engine**: The kernel orchestrates lifecycle, middleware define contracts
2. **Framework Agnostic**: No React, Vue, or UI concepts in kernel core
3. **Code-First Configuration**: `useMiddleware()` provides type safety and IDE support
4. **Error Isolation**: Failed FynApps don't crash the system ("party goes on")
5. **Timeout Enforcement**: Bootstrap dependencies time out after 30s

## UI Types in Middleware (Not Kernel)

The kernel returns `any` from `execute()` - it has no knowledge of UI rendering. Middleware packages define their own result contracts:

```typescript
// Shell middleware defines its result types (NOT in kernel)
// fynapp-shell-mw/src/middleware/shell-layout.ts
export type ShellExecutionResult =
  | { type: 'component-factory', componentFactory: (React: any) => any }
  | { type: 'rendered-content', content: string | HTMLElement }
  | { type: 'self-managed', container: HTMLElement }
  | { type: 'react-component', component: any, props?: any }
  | { type: 'render-function', render: (container: HTMLElement) => void };
```

FynApps can optionally import these types for compile-time safety:
```typescript
import type { ShellExecutionResult } from 'fynapp-shell-mw';

export const main = {
  execute(runtime): ShellExecutionResult {
    return { type: 'react-component', component: MyApp };
  }
};
```

## Extensibility Patterns

Middleware can define their own conventions for discovering additional FynUnits beyond `main`:

```typescript
// Shell middleware might look for routes
export const __routes__ = [
  { path: '/dashboard', component: Dashboard },
  { path: '/settings', component: Settings }
];

// Test middleware might look for test exports
export const __test__counter = { /* test config */ };

// Worker middleware might look for worker exports
export const __worker__processor = { /* worker config */ };
```

Each middleware becomes a mini-kernel for its domain, processing its own FynUnit conventions.

## See Also

- [Live demos](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/demo) and [guides](https://www.fynmesh.fyi/guides)
- [Execution Override Architecture](https://github.com/jchip/fynmesh/blob/main/core/kernel/design/execution-override-architecture.md)
- [FynApp Middleware Architecture](https://github.com/jchip/fynmesh/blob/main/core/kernel/design/fynapp-middleware-architecture.md)
- [Kernel Add-ons Design](https://github.com/jchip/fynmesh/blob/main/notes/KERNEL-ADDONS-DESIGN.md)
